ai.summary: The hourly impression limit for the Desktop-Billboard-Sidebar ad slot in `common/src/ads/billboard.ts` is reduced from 2 to 1 per rolling hour. This change tightens the frequency cap to prevent a campaign from spending its daily allowance too quickly in a single sitting. Regular users will see slightly fewer repeated ads in the sidebar during an hour, but no other parts of the app change.

ai.title: Sites local bundler names missing relative paths and adds desktop
ai.summary: The local Sites bundler in `common/src/sites/local-files.ts` now distinguishes missing files from containment violations in `localPath`, returning specific 'Site file not found' errors for relative paths inside the workspace while preserving the existing refusal for absolute or external paths. Concurrently, `common/src/desktop-cloud/hosted-workspace.ts` adds `sitesContext` and `sitesPublish` optional methods to the `HostedWorkspaceHost` interface, allowing the desktop app to read local site compatibility and trigger local build streaming for the Publish button. These changes are supported by new tests verifying that relative manifest paths resolve correctly and that missing files are named in error messages without exposing the absolute root.
ai.evidence: The diff modifies `common/src/sites/local-files.ts` to add `outside` and `missing` helpers and rework `localPath` to catch ENOENT/ENOTDIR errors, and modifies `common/src/desktop-cloud/hosted-workspace.ts` to add `sitesContext` and `sitesPublish` methods to `HostedWorkspaceHost`.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the native Electron implementation of the new `sitesContext` and `sitesPublish` host methods.

eli5.text: The desktop app now has the setup to let you build and publish websites directly from a chat that is running on your own computer. The process for gathering your local project files was also improved so that if a file is missing, the error message clearly names the specific folder it tried to find it in, rather than giving a generic warning. This affects you if you use the desktop version of the app to manage local projects; for most people, this is internal preparation for a new feature and does not change how your current sessions or free credits work.

The `refundPending` state now includes the note that each session keeps one hour of its price, and the zero-refund case explicitly states that refunds never refill a daily allowance that is already used up. entries.title: New shared/core files landed
entries.summary: New files: `common/src/desktop-rollout.ts`.

ai.title: Add shared utilities for staged desktop release rollouts
ai.summary: A new module in `common/` provides the read, write, and planning logic for staged Freebuff Desktop rollouts. The mechanism encodes rollout state (version and percentage) as a single hidden HTML comment in GitHub release notes, avoiding the race condition of replacing release assets. The planning function ensures that an in-progress rollout continues through subsequent releases with the original `since` version unless explicitly moved. Validation logic throws on unreadable markers to prevent accidentally offering a staged build to all installs.
ai.evidence: The diff adds a new file `common/src/desktop-rollout.ts` defining the `DesktopRollout` type and functions `formatDesktopRolloutMarker`, `readDesktopRolloutMarker`, `writeDesktopRolloutMarker`, and `planDesktopReleaseRollout` for managing staged desktop updates via hidden release notes markers.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the implementation of the reader in the web service or the writer script that consume these utilities yet.

eli5.text: The team added a new internal tool to manage the gradual release of the desktop app update. This mechanism ensures that a partial update keeps applying through future fixes without anyone needing to manually remember to extend it, preventing the app from accidentally offering a new version to everyone at once. This is internal engineering work that does not change how you use the app or what you see on your screen today.

ai.summary: The end-to-end test suite in `freebuff/e2e/tests/live-turn.e2e.test.ts` was updated to handle model rows with shared name prefixes. The test logic now explicitly asserts that the cursor does not land on these variant rows when targeting the base model, ensuring accurate simulation of the `/model` picker navigation.
